# shaneholmes10.github.io

Personal website and blog, built on the [al-folio](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio) Jekyll theme. Live at https://shaneholmes10.github.io

## Local development

```bash
docker compose pull && docker compose up
# site runs at http://localhost:8080
```

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the full dev workflow (formatting, pre-commit checklist, config notes).

## Generating the CV PDF

**Important:** the live CV (`assets/pdf/cv.pdf`) is generated by the custom `build_cv.py` script, not by `rendercv render` directly and not by the `.github/workflows/render-cv.yml` GitHub Action. Those both use RenderCV's default `classic` Typst theme, which looks nothing like the actual CV (blue text, centered header, no auto-fit) — that workflow has never actually produced the live PDF.

`build_cv.py` instead:

1. Reads `_data/cv.yml` directly, in its own schema (`label`, `studyType`, `title`/`awarder`, `keywords`, etc.) — you never hand-edit a RenderCV-schema file
2. Translates it in-memory into RenderCV's actual schema (`headline`, `degree`, `OneLineEntry`-style skills/awards, etc.)
3. Renders using the `engineeringresumes` RenderCV theme (not `classic`)
4. Tries a ladder of spacing/margin/font-size presets — roomy down to very tight — re-rendering until it finds the smallest preset that fits the content onto a whole number of pages, so nothing gets awkwardly cut off mid-page

### Usage

```bash
pip install "rendercv[full]" pyyaml pypdf
python3 build_cv.py _data/cv.yml --output assets/pdf/cv.pdf
```

Run this any time `_data/cv.yml` changes, then commit the regenerated `assets/pdf/cv.pdf`.
